tests.notes: TypeScript completed successfully. The focused ScrollReveal suite passed 5/5, covering one-time observer completion, focus completion, no-observer fallback, effective reduced motion, and distinct variants. Observer-completed and focus-completed instances remain revealed through reduced-motion on/off transitions without another observe call; an instance initially mounted under reduced motion remains visibly final and is never observed when motion is later re-enabled. The latest production Vite build passed after the document-clearance correction, and the focused mobile-dock Playwright regression passed. Earlier focused Vitest and full Playwright coverage passed the reveal, SaaS positioning, reduced-motion, all-staff-route, complete Maria journey, and caregiver clinical-data exclusion scenarios.

notes_for_next_agent: The reveal primitive uses IntersectionObserver progressive enhancement, unobserves completed targets, promotes focused content immediately, renders final content without observer support or under either reduced-motion source, and treats any final visibility path as terminal for that mounted instance so motion preference changes cannot hide or replay content.
The SaaS section states the buyer, subscribed capability, configuration shape, and expansion path without pricing, fabricated integrations, or demo/prototype framing.
Clinical Glass tokens now cover public, gateway, patient, staff, caregiver, system, modal, navigation, and mobile-dock surfaces while preserving operational labels and workflow semantics.

Fixed body backgrounds, broad repeated blur, the staff nested vertical scroller, and eager live-map mounting were removed or bounded; the document owns workspace scrolling and the stable map fallback remains available.
Caregiver rendering remains transportation-only, and browser coverage confirms clinical symptom text is absent after the staff resolution flow.

The mobile Workspace dock now uses explicit 44x44 CSS-pixel interactive targets while retaining compact 16px icons, accessible labels, visible focus styling, safe-area spacing, mobile no-overflow behavior, and the existing desktop breakpoint behavior.

The shared mobile app shell reserves document-end clearance for the fixed dock footprint, viewport offset, focus ring, and safe area; the footer motion control is fully visible and hit-testable above the dock at both required mobile widths.
